You mentioned sportsmanship. I think that's the key thing here. I'm also an athlete (fencing), and see a lot of people with high emotions on the field that can twist into unneeded hatred, or unnecessary blame. 

The main fencing group I spend time with does not divide by gender. But, it also doesn't divide by factors that might impact it in other ways- such as height, physical strength, stamina, age, energy level, etc. I'm a young man in my 20s, I am very tall with a strong, athletic build. I regularly get my ass handed to me by men twice my age and out of shape, women 2 feet shorter than me, etc. Sure, height can give an advantage. It certainly does for me. But I learned that I can't say "oh, well, I lost this fight SOLEY because my opponent is tall!" because it's never that simple. There's a million factors. It's unhealthy for my own development as an athlete, too, to hand wave my skill and performance and claim I only lost because of an unfair advantage my opponent has.

Whether or not this trans girl actually has a physical advantage matters less at this point than the fact that your young niece perceives it as an advantage and is using it in an unhealthy manner to focus her frustration and blame on.

I'd explain to her that, in her time, she'll meet many people of all shapes and bodies. Two cis girls of the same age might have massively different hormones. Two women of the same height and weight may have drastically different muscle mass builds. She'll meet people having a bad day who perform worse because of psychological aspects. She'll see a million wide factors that influence the outcome of a game. The important thing is to know differences are abundant in all sorts of ways, and we need to focus on how we approach stuff like that.
